why.heading: Why it exists
body: If you drive to cover roads, the question after a few weeks is always the same: which streets have I already driven, in which direction, and what is still missing nearby. A trip log does not answer it, and a map app forgets every drive.
Spur keeps every drive on the phone, matches it to the road network, and turns the result into a map of what you covered and routes over what you did not.
why.highlight: No account, no server, no analytics.

items.title: Records every drive
items.body: High-accuracy GPS in the background and with the screen locked. Raw fixes are kept exactly as recorded.

items.title: Roads by direction
items.body: Amber for one direction, green for both, divided and frontage roads counted as one road, plus a heatmap of every pass.

items.title: Plans what is left
items.body: Search streets and places, see how much you drove, and plan loops or routes to a goal over roads you have not driven.

items.title: Measures the drive
items.body: Braking, acceleration, cornering, bumps and road surface from the motion sensors, live and per trip.

items.title: Honest about gaps
items.body: A GPS gap stays a gap. The likely road across it is a suggestion you accept or reject, and the recording never changes.

items.title: Exports everything
items.body: GPX, CSV, GeoJSON, JSON, the raw motion samples, or every trip as one ZIP.

install.heading: Read the source
install.intro: Spur is not on the App Store. The source is public to be read; it is not licensed for use.

steps.title: Clone
steps.body: Swift 6 and SwiftUI, Apple frameworks only, no packages.

steps.title: Generate the project
steps.body: The Xcode project is generated from project.yml with XcodeGen.

steps.title: Run the tests
steps.body: More than 370 unit tests on an iOS 26 simulator.
steps.command: xcodebuild -project Spur.xcodeproj -scheme Spur -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' test

install.note: AGENTS.md in the repository explains the layout, the scripts and the rules the code follows.
